business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (single unitary national jurisdiction administered by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones 'GAFI' and the Egyptian Companies Authority 'ECA'; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (civil-law codified system of French tradition with an autonomous State Council/Conseil d'Etat administrative judiciary and limited application of Islamic Sharia principles in personal status and financial transactions; unitary national system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt–United States Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982, in force 1992)
Egypt–United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (1975, as applied following Brexit transitional arrangements)
Egypt–People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1994, in force 1995)
Egypt–United Arab Emirates Bilateral Investment Treaty
Egypt–EU Association Agreement (in force 2004, including establishment and investment protection chapters)
Treaty Establishing the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA, signed in Cairo 1993)
Agadir Free Trade Agreement among Egypt, Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia (in force 2007)
Unified Agreement for the Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab Countries (League of Arab States framework)
Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA) Convention (Egypt is a member)
New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (Egypt acceded in 1959)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Law No. 36 of 2024 and implemented by Executive Regulations issued under Prime Ministerial Decree No. 1432 of 2003, as amended, with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit 'EMLCU' established by Decree No. 1648 of 2005); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, mandating the maintenance and filing of a statutory Ultimate Beneficial Owner register); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2316 of 2017) governing GAFI incorporation procedures and UBO disclosure forms; Law No. 8 of 2015 on Regulating Terrorist Entities and Terrorists' Funds (terrorist designation list, asset freezing and reporting duties); Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law) and all Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT circulars applicable to banks and payment aggregators; Financial Regulatory Authority 'FRA' decisions and rulebooks extending UBO and AML/CFT obligations to non-banking financial institutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney granted by each foreign shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner to the Egyptian formation counsel and the designated Egyptian LLC manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's state of residence, countersigned by the competent certification authority (e.g. apostille authority or consular affairs office) of that state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Egypt has been a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention since 14 December 2022) OR Consular Legalization at the Embassy or Consulate of the Arab Republic of Egypt in the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of each corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles of association, and the board resolution approving the formation of the Egyptian LLC and its authorized signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent commercial registrar in the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by certified Arabic translation before an accredited sworn translator and attestation by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration covering the proposed initial capital contribution and expected operational funding for the ghost kitchen entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank's authorized officer in the origin country, with notarial attestation of the bank officer's signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required by the receiving Egyptian bank or the Central Bank of Egypt for in-bound transfer verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized sworn statement of ultimate beneficial ownership, executed by each UBO, disclosing ownership percentage, control structure, source of wealth, and confirmation of no Politically Exposed Person status unless declared
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the UBO's jurisdiction of residence or an Egyptian notary public where the UBO appears personally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, with the EMLCU-accepted format and subsequent filing through the GAFI incorporation module

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, proposed directors/managers, UBOs and authorized signatories against the Egyptian Council of Ministers terrorist entities and terrorists list issued under Law No. 8 of 2015, the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (ISIL/AQ and 1988 regimes), the OFAC SDN list applied because payment rails include USD-denominated aggregator payouts through UberEats and DoorDash, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list applicable to UK-linked counterparties, and MENAFATF/FATF public statements. Under Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended, obliged entities including banks, the EMLCU, notaries and GAFI apply enhanced due diligence to PEPs, their family members and close associates; any positive hit must be reported to the EMLCU through the approved electronic reporting portal within the statutory deadline. The LLC must retain complete UBO, PEP and sanctions-screening records for at least five years after the end of the business relationship and must refresh the screening at each financing round, manager appointment or ownership transfer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Electronic Services Platform — company incorporation and name-reservation module operated by the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones ('GAFI') at www.investin.gov.eg, integrated with the GAFI-run Commercial Registry database (Misr Commercial Registry) of the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Articles 9 and 195 of Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and applicable executive regulations, the statutory name of an Egyptian LLC must be in Arabic. A foreign-investor LLC may add a reversible, faithful transliteration in Roman/Latin script provided it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name or an earlier-registered trademark, and the name may not include any expression implying state affiliation, public purpose, a licensed banking/insurance activity, or a business line that the company will not actually operate. The Arabic name must be distinctive and must not contradict public order or religious sensitivities. Prior trademark clearance is required where the ghost kitchen trades under a virtual brand name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: الهيئة العامة (General Authority) — implies state agency
بنك (Bank) and صرافة (Currency Exchange) — reserved to Central Bank of Egypt-licensed entities
تأمين (Insurance) — reserved to Financial Regulatory Authority-licensed insurers
جيش (Army), شرطة (Police), قوات مسلحة (Armed Forces) — military connotation prohibited
رئيس الجمهورية (President of the Republic) — personal dignity protection
الإسلام or المسجد — religious tokens requiring special clearance and avoiding misleading religious connotation
القاهرة الكبرى (Greater Cairo), مصر (Egypt), الدلتا (Delta) — geographic tokens suggesting state domicile or conflicting with registered Nile Delta brands
وطني (National) — suggests state-owned enterprise without ministerial consent
استشاري or طبي — professional titles implying regulated practice absent a relevant license
مدن (Cities) — implies governorate or municipal administrative authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI issues a name-refusal notice, the applicant, through its Egyptian counsel, may file a written reconsideration request with GAFI's Central Administration for Companies within 15 working days of the refusal, attaching where relevant a trademark coexistence authorization, a ministerial approval for sensitive tokens, or a corrected transliteration. A second administrative refusal may be appealed within 60 days before the competent administrative court of the Egyptian State Council (Conseil d'Etat) in accordance with the grievance rules of the Executive Regulations of Law No. 159 of 1981. In parallel, the applicant may immediately submit a new name application containing three fallback names electronically on the GAFI portal, which typically obtains clearance faster than the judicial route. A cleared name is valid for 180 days and may be renewed for one further 180-day period by written request before expiry; if the reservation lapses, the applicant must re-file and re-pay the GAFI name-reservation fee and the new application will be re-checked for conflicts.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute for the operating premises of a food-service business. The ghost kitchen activity (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722513) requires a physical, licensed commercial kitchen unit registered as the LLC's domicile and approved by the National Food Safety Authority (NFSA), the municipal premises-licensing directorate, the civil-defense fire-safety authority, and the Egyptian Commercial Registry. A virtual office may be used only as an auxiliary correspondence address after the primary physical kitchen premises are leased, tenancy-attested, and the operational licenses have been obtained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — estimated 75–90% probability of unannounced NFSA hygiene and food-safety inspections within the first 12 operational months, augmented by municipal health inspections, civil-defense fire-safety checks, labor-office visits upon license issuance, and re-inspections triggered by any customer complaint or food-safety incident.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and commercial name-reservation certificate (خطاب عدم التخصيص) issued through the GAFI electronic portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory GAFI fee schedule for electronic name-reservation and company-establishment services, converted at the prevailing Central Bank of Egypt selling rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation commercial registry check for domicile address and prior registered-name conflicts through the GAFI Commercial Registry database
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial registry fee schedule for pre-incorporation data verification and database extract (approximately EGP 1,000–3,500 before notarial fees)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Arabic translation of foreign corporate documents, powers of attorney, bank letters and source-of-funds declarations (sworn translators accredited before Egyptian courts, with Ministry of Foreign Affairs attestation where required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translation offices recognized by the Egyptian Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing sworn-translation market tariff of EGP 300–700 per page for a 10–14 page bundle, plus notarial countersignature

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Hague Apostille or Egyptian consular legalization of the core document bundle (three notarial sets covering POA, corporate resolutions, bank reference letters and UBO sworn statements)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the origin jurisdiction; apostille authority in the origin state; Embassy or Consulate of the Arab Republic of Egypt in the origin state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Diplomatic and consular fee schedules and apostille administrative tariffs, estimated at USD 60–180 per document for three core documents, excluding courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO profiling and AML/CFT pre-incorporation file preparation: PEP, OFAC, UN and Egyptian terrorist-list screening reports for all proposed shareholders, managers and UBOs, with a written CDD memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent AML/CFT compliance consultant or the instructed Egyptian law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee of USD 400–700 for a complete UBO and sanctions-screening review using accredited screening databases

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) eligibility review and food-safety-approach consultation for the ghost kitchen premises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed food-safety engineering consultant coordinating the NFSA pre-application dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing consulting-charge market benchmark for food-premises design review and NFSA pre-application consultation (non-statutory advisory fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment and notary-attested tenancy filing of the registered office/domicile letter (شهر عقاري) for the physical kitchen premises, including preliminary municipal zoning verification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Egyptian notary public and the local real-estate registration authority delegated by the competent municipal directorate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial and tenancy-registration fee schedule, plus prevailing mark-up for venue verification (approximately EGP 4,000–7,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel fee for structuring the LLC, drafting the Arabic memorandum of association and founders' contract, coordinating GAFI incorporation filings, UBO register submission, and attendance at the notary public on incorporation day
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Egyptian law firm admitted before the Egyptian Courts of Appeal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 1,200–3,500 for a standard Egyptian LLC formation with cross-border shareholders, excluding governmental fees and taxes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory document stamps, notarial certification fees and official publication costs (two insertions in Al-Waqa'i' Al-Masriya official gazette and one licensed daily economic newspaper)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff schedule for company incorporation extracts and the notarial fee schedule for certified copies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Emergency reserve for exchange-rate fluctuation and GAFI/notarial incidental fees during the incorporation window
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prudent benchmark of 5% of the aggregate estimated pre-incorporation budget to absorb fee-schedule revisions and EGP exchange-rate movement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, Articles 1, 3, 7, 14 and 24; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Code No. 17 of 1999.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) — Companies Registration and One-Stop Shop Department
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Formal Incorporation Application and Certificate of Incorporation issued by GAFI (Certificate of Qayd)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an LLC under Egyptian Companies Law; the declared paid-up capital must be fully evidenced by a bank deposit certificate or an in-kind contribution valuation approved by GAFI, and the total subscribed capital may be paid within five years from incorporation, except for cash contributions which must be paid at the time of formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of [EG_LLC] hereby approves the subscription of shares by the founding members in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles of Association; adopts the registered office located at [address in Cairo/Governorate] as the official domicile of the Company; and appoints [Name A] as Managing Director, [Name B] as Finance Director, and [Name C] as Compliance Officer, each with such authority and duties as specified in the Articles. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Managing Director is authorized to complete all statutory filings with GAFI, open the corporate bank account, execute the formation agreements, and take all necessary steps to obtain the food facility operating license and civil defense clearances.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Legal Entity Examination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Electronic Portal / GAFI One-Stop Shop Name Reservation Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through GAFI's electronic portal, selecting the legal form 'Limited Liability Company' and the ISIC code 5610 for food services. Provide the proposed Arabic trade name and a transliterated English, verify unavailability, pay the nominal reservation fee, and download the conditional name certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of each founding member's national ID or passport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected, file a written objection with GAFI's names committee and simultaneously submit one alternative name to avoid statutory delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public Office (Katib Al-Adl) attached to GAFI or the competent notarization directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic-language Memorandum and Articles of Association using the GAFI-approved template for LLCs. All founders or their notarially appointed attorney-in-fact must sign every page in the presence of the notary. The registered office address must be stated and accepted, and the founding board members must sign a statement of their consent to serve.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney if a representative signs
Copy of each founder's valid ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies inconsistency, execute a notarial supplementary correction or re-submit an amended version; a typographic error can be rectified by a marginal notarial correction without full re-execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening a Temporary Capital Deposit Account and Obtaining Paid-up Capital Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed Egyptian commercial bank, typically National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, or a private-sector bank with GAFI integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate formation account in the company's name and deposit the declared paid-up capital. Obtain a certified statement from the bank setting out the depositor names, deposit date, and total amount. Retain the bank certificate for submission to GAFI as conclusive evidence of capital payment.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copies of authorized signatories
Board consent to the temporary bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account because of incomplete KYC, complete the additional source-of-funds declaration immediately; if capital cannot be deposited in the prescribed period, revise the schedule of paid-up capital in the Articles and obtain prior GAFI approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission to GAFI and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / GAFI Digital Incorporation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the full incorporation dossier in the GAFI online single-window system within 30 days of notarization. Pay the statutory filing fee and any applicable electronic clearing fees. GAFI will verify the capital certificate, legal form, and constituted bodies and will issue the electronic incorporation certificate and company operating number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of lawful activity under ISIC 5610
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a query, respond through the portal within five business days; if the application is formally rejected, appeal to the GAFI Review Committee within 15 days and provide corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSII)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation is complete, apply electronically for a corporate tax card, VAT registration if turnover threshold is met or expected, and withholding tax registration. Simultaneously register the company and its employees with the social insurance authority using the incorporation certificate and payroll data.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles and registered office lease
List of founding directors and their IDs
Initial payroll register for social insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA or NOSI requests additional legalization, file an immediate rectification application at the relevant service center and provide certified Arabic copies; any issuing error should be corrected by an official decision within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Listing and Official Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent Commercial Registry Office in the Governorate where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the registration deed to the Commercial Registry to obtain the final commercial register extract and commercial registration number. Pay the publication fee and arrange summary publication in the official gazette; the commercial registration serves as conclusive third-party evidence of the company's existence and capacity.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease contract of registered office
Board power of attorney for the registration manager
Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects the lease address or officer identity, furnish the street-numeric specification certificate and re-submit the corrected dossier; appeal a substantive refusal to the competent administrative court if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Facility Operating License, Civil Defense Clearance and Environmental Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Food Safety Authority (NFSA), General Civil Defense Authority, and Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency, coordinated at the local governorate licensing center
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the ghost-kitchen floor plan, food-safety management plan, and lease contract to the NFSA one-stop shop; undergo a premises inspection for zoning, sanitation, ventilation, waste disposal and structural compliance. Obtain a Civil Defense fire-safety certificate after inspection of alarms, extinguishers, emergency exits and exhaust systems. Register the facility with the environmental authority under the applicable low-impact category and secure the environmental clearance certificate before commencing delivery-only food production.
required_dossiers: Commercial register extract and tax card
Notarized lease of the kitchen premises
Detailed floor plan with equipment layout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any cited non-conformities regarding fire equipment, exhaust ducts, sewage connections or food-storage areas within the authority's quarantine period; thereafter request a technical re-inspection. If the license is conditionally denied, appeal to the licensing appeals committee within 30 days with the remedial work permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) — Food Establishment Licensing Department; coordinated with the General Organization for Physical Planning and the Ministry of Supply for food-service facilities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operating License — Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Limited Environmental Impact; the ghost kitchen must complete Environmental Registration Form A1 and submit a scoping summary; a Full EIA Report is required only for central kitchens exceeding 5,000 meals per day or for kitchen facilities situated in sensitive catchment zones.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: wastewater pH 6–9, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) ≤ 60 mg/L, total suspended solids (TSS) ≤ 60 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L; cooking-exhaust volatile organic compounds (VOCs) ≤ 0.1 mg/m³; particulate matter ≤ 10 mg/m³; odour must be neutralized to protect adjacent land uses; solid waste and grease-trap residues must be collected by licensed waste-management operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Civil Defense fire-safety clearance covering automatic fire detection, portable extinguishers, safety exits, and fire dampers on exhaust ducts; a structural inspection by a licensed engineer confirming the floor load capacity for installed cooking equipment; an occupational health certificate for food handlers based on medical examination; and approval of the emergency evacuation plan and gas-shutoff system for the delivery-only kitchen.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance; unified tax registration and e-services portal: https://www.tax.gov.eg; mandatory government e-invoicing platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For an Egyptian LLC, the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN / Tax Card) is issued through the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) one-stop-shop at incorporation; the entity must then activate its tax file with the competent ETA office and complete VAT registration (Law 67/2016) within 30 days of commencing taxable activity or immediately once annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000. A foreign entity without local incorporation obtains a non-resident TIN/VAT ID via direct application at the ETA Large Taxpayer Center or through a fiscal representative when it creates a permanent establishment in Egypt; registration must be completed before the first taxable supply or invoice is issued. The unified TIN governs CIT, VAT, withholding tax, stamp duty, and e-invoicing obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or entity classification election exists under Egyptian law; classification is statutorily determined, and an LLC is mandatorily a separate taxable person subject to corporate income tax under Law 91/2005 as amended by Law 30/2023. Available elections include (i) choice of depreciation method for fixed assets under the Income Tax Law; (ii) application for an Advance Pricing Agreement (APA) under Article 56 of Law 91/2005 for transfer pricing certainty; (iii) formal election for special economic zone / free zone incentives (e.g., Suez Canal Economic Zone) at the licensing stage; and (iv) group companies are taxed as separate entities with no consolidated filing election. Hybrid mismatch rules have not been enacted, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Article 52 of Law 91/2005) and transfer pricing articles empower the ETA to recharacterize artificial structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Law No. 67 of 2016 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 (annual taxable turnover of goods and services) for mandatory registration; voluntary registration is available from EGP 50,000; non-resident suppliers with a fixed establishment, branch, or permanent establishment in Egypt must register irrespective of the turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Statutory B2B e-invoicing is mandatory for all ETA-registered taxpayers under Law 67/2016 as amended by Law 26/2020 and implementing ETA decisions. Invoices must be transmitted in XML (UBL 2.1) to the government e-invoicing platform (einvoicing.eta.gov.eg), digitally signed with the taxpayer's ETA-issued digital certificate, and processed through the regulated API/PSD integration. The ETA performs real-time validation and clearance and returns a QR-coded stamped invoice that the buyer must accept before posting; paper or non-cleared invoices are fiscally invalid. Phased B2C e-receipt mandates also apply to retail and delivery transactions, including restaurant and cloud kitchen sales via aggregator platforms, with non-compliance triggering penalties under Law 67/2016 and the unified tax procedure rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies under Article 21 of Law 67/2016 to (i) goods physically exported from Egypt to a non-resident buyer, including food products and kitchen supplies if actually shipped and removed from the Egyptian customs territory; and (ii) offshore services rendered to a non-resident recipient and economically consumed outside Egypt, subject to the substantiation conditions of Executive Regulation Decree 66/2017. The Egyptian LLC must maintain a complete export file evidencing contract, shipment, and foreign currency proceeds; domestic sales through delivery aggregator platforms such as UberEats/Careem and DoorDash remain standard-rated supplies at 14% VAT and cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (ACI/Nafeza S-Declaration or C4 certificate) evidencing removal from the Egyptian customs territory
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or multimodal transport document issued to the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list in Arabic/English matching the customs declaration
Sales contract or purchase order naming the non-resident counterparty
Foreign currency inward remittance certificate (bank credit advice, T/T, or D/A-D/P settlement certificate) confirming proceeds repatriation through an Egyptian bank
ETA export VAT refund claim file and zero-rating register reconciled with e-invoicing records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA conducts pre-refund desk audits of export claims, cross-checking customs data (ACI/Nafeza), transport documents, and bank FX records; refunds are normally payable within 45 days of a complete application, with statutory delay interest where exceeded. If export documentation, shipment, or FX repatriation is defective, the zero-rating is retroactively revoked and 14% VAT is clawed back with interest from the original filing date, plus a monthly delay penalty of 2% and fines of up to 100% of evaded tax under Law 67/2016 Articles 38-42; submission of forged or false documents triggers criminal prosecution, imprisonment, blacklisting by the ETA, and loss of export refund privileges. The GAAR (Article 52 of Law 91/2005) further permits recharacterization of circular or sham export arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), the sole monetary and foreign-exchange authority under Law No. 88 of 2003 as amended by Law No. 194 of 2020, acting through its Foreign Exchange Market Regulations, Unified Banking Rules, and AML/CFT framework. CBE-licensed commercial banks are the only permitted counterparties for corporate FX dealing, statutory reporting, and cross-border remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; current-account transactions are freely settleable at the interbank market rate. Capital-account transactions are formally liberalized for foreign direct investment in Egyptian LLCs, with 100% non-resident ownership permitted. Profit and dividend remittances are executed through licensed banks using CBE declaration forms, supported by audited financial statements, Egyptian Tax Authority clearance, and proof that the investment was registered with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI). The 2022-2024 FX shortage period caused de facto rationing and a parallel-market premium; following the March 2024 exchange-rate unification and IMF-supported stabilization, convertibility for trade and investment flows has normalized, though banks retain enhanced due-diligence discretion over the source of EGP liquidity. The LLC must maintain a complete documentary trail of inward shareholder funds, EGP tax compliance, and audited financial records to withstand any future FX-rationing inquiry.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Unified Foreign Exchange Rules, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into an Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the shipment date (bill of lading or airway bill) or, for services, within 90 days from the invoice date, unless the CBE approves an extension. There is currently no fixed statutory percentage of mandatory conversion into EGP; exporters may retain proceeds in a domestic foreign-currency account or sell them through the interbank market. Documentary prerequisites include the export customs declaration, commercial invoice, transport document, and, where applicable, the settlement statement of the foreign delivery platform. Hard-currency receipts of the ghost-kitchen LLC from offshore aggregators such as DoorDash or UberEats USD settlement legs are subject to the same 90-day repatriation rule; local EGP collections from Egyptian platforms do not constitute export proceeds for this regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Deposit / Pre-Incorporation Certificate Account and EGP Operational Current Account
Capital Deposit / Pre-Incorporation Certificate Account and EGP Operational Current Account
Capital Deposit Account, EGP Operational Current Account, and USD Concentration Account for Aggregator Settlements
EGP Operational Account and Multicurrency Foreign-Currency Account under HSBC Global Documentation Standards

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for use as the primary statutory treasury account; Medium only as a documented settlement bridge for foreign aggregator payouts. An Egyptian LLC must maintain its paid-up capital deposit, operational payroll, and FX-repatriation flows with a CBE-licensed bank. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut Business are not CBE-licensed banks and cannot issue the statutory capital-deposit certificate or process CBE-regulated remittances. Balances parked offshore beyond the 90-day repatriation window may be characterized as an unapproved export retention, attracting AML red flags. If an EMI is used, it must be registered under the provider's own KYC process, and every sweep to the Egyptian bank must be accompanied by the relevant platform settlement report and payment purpose code.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical presence is required at the corporate account-opening interview. CBE AML/CFT rules and the Unified KYC Regulations require the local legal representative and at least one authorized signatory to appear in-branch for identity verification; the ultimate beneficial owner must be identified and may be interviewed by video-KYC, but remote-only account opening is not available at tier-1 Egyptian banks. A non-resident director may delegate authority only through an Egyptian consulate-certified or apostilled notarized power of attorney appointing an Egypt-resident manager, with certified Arabic translation. The minimum onboarding timeline including document legalization is approximately 10-15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified operating premise for a delivery-only cloud kitchen with no customer-facing restaurant address or shared-commissary occupancy.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed lease contract for the kitchen or commissary, utility bills for the preceding 12 months, municipal commercial-activity license, National Food Safety Authority (NFSA) registration, food-handling permits for each virtual brand, and dated exterior/interior photographs of the production premises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners resident in, or citizenship-linked to, a FATF-Monitored, OFAC-sanctioned, or High-Risk Third Country.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence permit of each UBO, certified source-of-wealth statement, bank reference letter from the parent-company bank, SWIFT inward remittance evidence funding the capital, apostilled corporate register extract, and an independent sanctions-screening report confirming no match on UN, US OFAC, EU, and UK HMT consolidated lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-value marketplace settlement lines from UberEats, Talabat, or DoorDash perceived as opaque pass-through activity with third-party PSPs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed delivery-aggregator agreements, monthly platform payout settlement statements displaying order-level IDs and net settlement amounts, a reconciliation sub-ledger reviewed by the statutory auditor, ETA e-invoice and e-receipt records for each settled meal, and approved merchant-descriptor registrations on each platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Paid-in capital structure reliant on shareholder loans, cash deposits, or in-kind contributions that impede clean measurement of the foreign investment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-to-bank SWIFT wire receipt for the equity tranche, share-subscription agreement, board capital-call resolution, statutory auditor's capital-verification certificate, CBE/GAFI inward-investment reporting card, and a valuation report compliant with Egyptian Valuation Standards for any in-kind portion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty or technical-fee flows to a foreign virtual-brand owner raising transfer-pricing and treaty-abuse questions on outbound remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal virtual-brand license or franchise agreement in Arabic notarized form, arm's-length royalty benchmark study or advance pricing agreement, Egyptian withholding-tax receipts on outbound royalties, and the parent group's beneficial-ownership chart with full chain-of-ownership documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires an SWIFT MT103, or MT202 COV for nostro-mediated tranches, from the foreign parent to the LLC's pre-incorporation deposit account at a CBE-licensed bank. The remittance narrative must include the GAFI incorporation-file number, the CBE balance-of-payments purpose classification for Direct Investment Equity, and the LLC's future Egyptian tax identification number. The receiving bank issues the statutory capital-deposit certificate, which is a mandatory annex to the Commercial Registry application. After the Commercial Registry certificate is issued, the pre-incorporation account is converted into the permanent EGP operating account, and shareholder funds may be converted into EGP at the interbank rate. Subsequent injections by way of share premium or shareholder loan must be recorded in the bank's transaction-monitoring system and in the CBE's FDI and external-debt reporting gateway; shareholder loans require registration to permit later interest and principal repatriation without adverse FX characterization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury flows for operating expenses such as bulk raw-food procurement, cloud-kitchen software subscriptions, aggregator commissions, royalties, and freight are settled through: (1) SWIFT MT103 direct remittances under open-account trading terms; (2) documentary commercial letters of credit issued per UCP600 via SWIFT MT700 for larger imported inventory and equipment; and (3) SWIFT MT202 COV where clearing is effected through nostro relationships. Each outbound payment must cite the underlying contract and invoice, an ETA-compliant e-invoice or e-receipt, the customs ACID import record for physical goods, and a tax-clearance or withholding certificate where Egyptian WHT applies to royalties, technical-service fees, or interest. Aggregator commission payments to offshore platform groups must be supported by the marketplace agreement and the platform's settlement statement. Purpose codes follow the CBE balance-of-payments reporting manual: goods in the 100-series, services and commissions in the 200-series, income in the 300-series, and transfers in the 400-series.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EGP/USD forward contract with a maximum tenor of approximately 12 months, supported by an authenticated underlying trade or investment exposure and margin or collateral per bank credit policy
Onshore FX swap combining a spot and forward leg between EGP and USD or EUR to match working-capital receivable and payable timing of aggregator settlements
Cross-currency swap between EGP and USD or EUR for medium-term balance-sheet hedging, requiring CBE transaction approval and documented foreign-investment or trade-flow cover
OTC European-style FX options offered by tier-1 banks for hedging forecasted aggregator revenues, subject to non-speculative underwriting and periodic position reporting

Offshore non-deliverable EGP forwards are not directly available to the resident LLC without a CBE license; the permissible onshore equivalent is the deliverable forward, while NDFs operate only among non-resident counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 41) with audited financial statement attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar fiscal year; return due within 4 months of year-end (by 30 April following the tax year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EGP 5,000 - 20,000 under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005; late-payment interest at 2% per month on unpaid tax; ETA enforcement, bank account seizure, and criminal liability; no direct administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements and Shareholders' Assembly Approval Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment (GAFI), Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements prepared within 3 months of year-end; shareholders' assembly convened within 6 months; approved statements filed with GAFI within 30 days of assembly approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managerial fines and disqualification; GAFI may administratively dissolve or strike off the LLC for two consecutive years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal on the registration anniversary date; application submitted within the final 30 days before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating monthly late fees; suspension of trading status after 3 months of delinquency; deletion from the Commercial Register and administrative strike-off for persistent non-renewal

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI UBO and AML Compliance Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation concurrent with Commercial Registry renewal; interim UBO update within 30 days of any shareholding transfer or ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines for inaccurate, incomplete, or late UBO disclosures under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended; refusal to renew registration and freezing of corporate records

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all LLCs regardless of turnover or capital; the shareholders' assembly must appoint at least one Egyptian licensed auditor to examine the annual financial statements and issue a statutory audit report
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), substantially converged with IFRS and issued by the Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a UBO register and reconfirm it annually with GAFI at Commercial Registry renewal; every shareholding transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members, registered in the Commercial Registry, and reflected in the UBO register within 30 days of the transfer

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (current statutory rate on commercial, industrial and service profits under Law No. 91 of 2005 Art. 51, as amended by Law No. 30 of 2023; the pre-amendment rate for earlier fiscal years was 22.5%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free-zone and SCZONE entities: 0% CIT on income from sources outside Egypt and on export-related operations subject to Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; small and micro enterprises under Law No. 152 of 2020: presumptive rates of 0.5% to 2% of gross turnover for qualifying businesses; inland investment projects in development areas: up to 50% investment-cost deduction from taxable income over 5 to 7 years; temporary additional 30% to 50% deduction of investment costs for technology-intensive and labour-intensive projects per Investment Law implementing regulations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form No. 45 (Corporate Income Tax Return for juridical persons) filed via the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) electronic filing portal at eta.gov.eg; final CIT payment is made through ETA bank collection vouchers or the national e-payment gateway
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; four quarterly advance CIT instalments are payable during the tax year and are reconciled against the final annual liability on Form No. 45
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return and final payment are due on or before the expiration of four months following the close of the company's fiscal year (Art. 56, Law No. 91 of 2005); for a calendar-year LLC the statutory deadline is 30 April; the ETA may grant an extension of up to 60 days upon justified application

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Egyptian tax card number, commercial registration number, head office address and the competent ETA tax office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian branch or permanent establishment (PE) completes this box in its own name using the ETA-issued tax card and the registered Egyptian branch address; a non-resident with no Egyptian PE and no Egyptian-sourced attributable profit does not file Form No. 45 and is instead subject to final withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year being declared, e.g. 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024; loss carry-forward and tax credit entries must relate to the same period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian branch/PE must align the filing period with its Egyptian accounting closing date and cannot adopt a different cut-off from the foreign head office without ETA approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal and secondary activities under the Egyptian activity classification; a delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen is recorded as ISIC 5610 food and beverage service activity and, for Egyptian tax purposes, as a commercial food-service activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must use the same ISIC 5610 classification as its Egyptian operating licence; the declared description 'virtual brand delivery kitchen' must correspond to the food-safety and commercial licences actually held in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Book Net Profit or Loss Before Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result per audited financial statements prepared under Egyptian Accounting Standards; gross delivery revenue from all digital platforms (UberEats, DoorDash-type payout rails, Talabat and similar aggregators) must be recorded gross, with platform commissions and rider costs presented as deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE books only Egyptian-sourced delivery revenue after intercompany settlement; head office allocations not supported by contemporaneous cost records and an arm's length analysis cannot be deducted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory disallowances under Art. 25, Law No. 91 of 2005, including personal withdrawals by shareholders, fines, income tax amounts, unrealised provisions, non-arms-length payments to related parties and a fixed statutory portion of general entertainment expenses; depreciation is computed under ETA schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back head-office management fees and virtual-brand royalty payments unless they satisfy the arm's length test, are supported by a transfer pricing file and the relevant withholding tax has been deducted and remitted; otherwise the deduction and the transfer pricing position both fail.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Taxable Income and Loss Utilisation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back disallowed items and subtracting eligible tax losses; losses may be carried forward for five tax years only and no carry-back is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may offset only losses attributable to its Egyptian activities; foreign head-office losses are not available against Egyptian taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of CIT at the 25% commercial rate on taxable income; any free-zone exemption, presumptive small-enterprise rate or investment incentive must be evidenced by an investment certificate or free-zone licence attached to the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A branch of a foreign company is taxed at the same 25% rate on Egyptian-source profits attributable to the PE; no deemed dividend deduction is allowable to the branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Advance Payments, Withholdings and Balance Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance CIT instalments, salaries tax withheld at source, service-contract withholding tax and tax certificates; the resulting net amount is payable with the filing of Form No. 45.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident payees may credit Egyptian withholding tax only where a treaty relief application has been formally accepted by the ETA; unapproved treaty claims must be pursued by refund application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Audited financial statements, tax depreciation schedules, related-party transaction schedules, transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File if thresholds exceeded), commercial and food-safety licences, e-invoice logs and the director's signed declaration of completeness.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must attach the Egyptian branch audit report, the head-office board resolution appointing the Egyptian tax representative and, where applicable, the DTA residence certificates for related-party payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000 per deficient return plus a monthly delinquency surcharge of 1% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month of delay; failure after formal notice can raise the surcharge, and deliberate concealment triggers criminal penalties of up to double the evaded tax together with prosecution before the Economic Courts.
